text: Internal media-buyer playbook. DSCR refinance only. Housing Special Ad Category — creative is the targeting. Stamp from draft after founder approval.
1. What you're optimizing for
You are not targeting demographics. You are sorting investors by what stops them from acting today. That constraint decides the message, the label, and the ad set.
Who: Real-estate investors who already own rentals. Operator energy. Not seniors. Not consumer relief.
Product: DSCR refinance only — business-purpose. The property qualifies on rent vs payment, not W-2s / tax returns / DTI.
Big idea: "The property qualifies itself." Honest trade: rates often higher than conventional — you win on access and process.
Governing question for every creative: What stops this investor from acting today? Not who they are. Not the property type. Not what they'd do with the money.
2. The four buckets
Three constraint buckets move people. One in-market lane harvests people already shopping. Every creative gets exactly one.

text: 3. How to sort any ad
Overlap is real (balloon + write-offs). Priority order makes buckets mutually exclusive so Mr. Waiz rollups stay clean.

caption: Check top to bottom — first yes wins

text: IN-MARKET is only for product-named + terms/spec creatives with no pain messaging. If the ad speaks to a constraint, it is never IN-MARKET.
Modifiers vs use cases (not buckets)
Modifiers (write-offs, STR, FN, property-count) change the example inside DENIED — same enemy, same job.
Use cases (pay off balloon, fund rehab, reserves, LLC) answer "what would you do with it?" — illustrate the ad; do not organize by them.
4. How to label every ad

caption: Four fields required before a concept ships or registers

dscr_{concept-slug}_{format}_v{n}

Examples:
  dscr_nodocs-speed_st_v1
  dscr_balloon-exit_ugc_v1
  dscr_cashout-grow_st_v1
  dscr_ratecard-centered_st_v1
Bucket + creative job live in overview / summary / tags — not inside the ad_name token.
One primary creative job per ad. Don't average reveal + authority into one bland concept.
Proven angles → home
* lo-authority / qualify-stack = proposed slugs — register before first use.
5. Campaign & ad set structure
Campaign = temperature + budget logic. Ad set = one bucket × one creative job. That is how you get a clean read under Andromeda.

caption: Launch shape — cold test earns reads; scale opens only after winners; warm owns shared jobs

text: One bucket × one job = one ad set = one primary creative. Do not dump three angles into one ad set.
Budget barbell (while proving)
~80% DENIED + DEADLINE (+ IN-MARKET terms if approved numbers exist).
~20% IDLE — belief-change lane; don't kill it on day-3 CPL alone, but it still needs a terminal CPQL + review date.
Warm authority opens when an engager pool exists — not as the only cold creative.
Don't build cold_scale until a concept hits your CPL threshold for 7 consecutive days.
How to judge each bucket

rows: Engagement / LP first, then CPQL with a kill date
CPQL, booked rate, show rate — not vanity CTR

text: 6. Media-buyer checklist
Read the creative. Run the sorting rule (deadline → denied → idle → in-market).
Fill four labels: bucket · creative_job · concept_slug · angle_ref.
Name the ad: dscr_{slug}_{format}_v{n}.
Place it in the matching ad set (one bucket × one job).
Cold numbers only if tokens are client-confirmed. Otherwise idea-first / number-free.
Never: purchase framing, guarantees, invented rates, RM/senior tone, literal "exclusive."
Cold launch order
When you need a starting slate: DENIED → DEADLINE → IDLE. Add IN-MARKET when the client's rate/spec sheet is approved for ads.
